AWL Agri Business.desc: Formerly Adani Wilmar, AWL is India's largest branded edible-oil player (Fortune oils) and a growing food-staples company with wheat flour, rice, pulses, sugar and ready-to-cook lines. Post the Adani Enterprises stake sale to Wilmar, the business is being repositioned as a pure-play branded-foods franchise with industry-leading distribution depth across 1 million+ outlets. Margin profile is thin and commodity-sensitive but mix is shifting toward value-added foods.

Adani Power.desc: India's largest private-sector thermal power generator with ~18 GW of operating capacity and a roadmap to ~31 GW by FY30E across coal-fired plants in Mundra, Tiroda, Kawai, Udupi, Raipur and Mahan. Earnings volatility has eased as merchant exposure shrinks — 95% of operating capacity is now tied up under long-term PPAs at improving tariffs. Capacity additions are largely equipment-locked at competitive rates with L&T and BHEL, supporting visibility on 20%+ EBITDA growth through FY30.

Afcons Infrastructure.desc: Flagship infrastructure-EPC arm of the Shapoorji Pallonji group, executing marine, urban-metro, hydro, oil & gas, surface-transport and underground projects across India, the Middle East, Africa and South Asia. Strong record on complex, technically-differentiated jobs (sea-link bridges, large-diameter tunnels, hydro caverns) drives an order book usually 3x trailing revenue. FY26 saw margin pressure and execution slowdown from West Asia tensions; FY27 outlook hinges on order conversion of the ~₹1.8tn pipeline.

Amber Enterprises.desc: India's largest room-AC contract manufacturer, supplying most major brands (Voltas, Daikin, LG, Samsung, Whirlpool) with finished ACs, components and increasingly electronics. The electronics (PCBA) and railway sub-systems verticals via Sidwal and ILJIN are scaling fast and now anchor the long-term growth story, with PCB facility commissioning a key near-term margin lever. Consumer-durable revenue is cyclical with the cooling season; FY27 margin profile is in a transitional dip.

Anthem Biosciences.desc: Bangalore-based contract research, development and manufacturing organisation serving global innovator pharma and biotech with small molecules, peptides, biologics and fermentation chemistry. Differentiated technology stack (one-stop NCE-to-commercial integration) and a long-tail customer book have delivered industry-leading 30%+ EBITDA margins. Recently listed; the China+1 thesis and biologics ramp-up underpin the growth case.

Astral.desc: India's #2 CPVC/PVC plumbing-pipes brand with growing presence in adhesives (Resinova), paints, water tanks, valves and bath-ware — pivoting toward a broader building-materials platform. Plumbing volumes grew >20% in Mar-Q on share gains and channel expansion, though the adhesives margin took a near-term hit from raw-material inflation. Long runway from housing under-penetration and unorganised-to-organised shift.

Avalon Technologies.desc: Vertically-integrated industrial EMS player with manufacturing in India and the US, focused on box-build for power, semiconductor, clean-energy, medical and aerospace customers. Differentiated by end-to-end PCBA-to-system assembly capability and proximity to US OEMs at a moment when nearshoring + AI-driven power capex are accelerating. Anchor-report initiation by Nomura highlights TAM expansion in HVDC, BESS and SPE.

Avenue Supermarts.desc: Operator of the DMart value-retail chain — India's most efficient hypermarket format with the lowest cost-to-serve in the listed retail universe. Slowed store additions hurt revenue growth in FY24-26, but FY26 saw +85 net new stores and 20% YoY network expansion, putting growth back on track. Like-for-like (LFL) recovery is the swing factor — sensitive to staples inflation and the disruption from quick-commerce in metros.

Bajaj Finserv.desc: Holding company of the Bajaj group's financial-services franchise — Bajaj Finance (consumer lending), Bajaj Allianz Life & General Insurance, and newer ventures in payments, broking and AMC. Core lending business continues to grow ~25% with stable asset quality; insurance subsidiaries are gaining market share. Investor focus has shifted to the new-ventures portfolio (which is near breakeven) and execution on the holdco discount.

Bharat Electronics.desc: Government-owned defence-electronics PSU and India's largest indigenous-radar, communication-systems and electronic-warfare supplier. Order book of ~₹70k cr provides 3-year revenue cover; civilian diversification into homeland security, space, civil aviation and semiconductor packaging widens the addressable market. Execution and margin are best-in-class among defence PSUs; near-term concerns are around order-inflow lumpiness post the surge in FY24-26.

Bharat Petroleum.desc: India's second-largest oil-marketing company with ~16% market share in fuel retail, plus refining capacity of ~38 mmtpa at Mumbai, Kochi and Bina. Earnings are driven by refining margins (GRMs) and marketing margins on auto fuels; LPG subsidy under-recoveries remain a structural drag. Big-ticket projects include the Bina petrochemical complex and city-gas expansion through Bharat Gas Resources.

CMS Info Systems.desc: India's largest cash-management company — ATM cash replenishment, cash-in-transit, retail cash management and managed services for banks. Diversifying into adjacent BFSI tech with the FSS acquisition (ATM-as-a-service, brown-label ATMs, software). Volume growth is steady; the moat is the unmatched logistics footprint across 25,000+ pin codes.

Carborundum Universal.desc: Murugappa-group leader in abrasives, ceramics and electro-minerals — a key supplier to automotive, infrastructure, energy and electronics OEMs in India and globally via subsidiaries in Russia, South Africa and the US. Core abrasives business is gaining share; loss-making overseas units are being restructured or exited. Long-term thesis is industrial-capex revival and import-substitution in technical ceramics.

Chalet Hotels.desc: K Raheja-promoted luxury and upscale hotel chain operating Marriott, Westin, JW Marriott, Renaissance and Hyatt Regency properties in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Pune. Beneficiary of the structural uptick in Indian leisure & business travel; ARRs and occupancies are at multi-year highs. Capacity addition pipeline of 800+ keys and the commercial real-estate annuity portfolio add to the growth optionality.

Coforge.desc: Midcap IT services exporter with deep verticals in BFSI, travel & transportation and insurance — and a strategic bet on AI-led platforms (Quasar) and large-deal execution. Acquired Cigniti to build a quality-engineering & AI competency at scale. Margins are in a transitional dip from integration, but order book and deal TCV growth lead the midcap pack.

Deepak Nitrite.desc: Integrated specialty-chemicals producer (phenol, acetone, IPA, fuel additives, performance chemicals) with India's only large-scale phenol-acetone complex at Dahej. Windfall margins on phenol are normalising as global supply restarts; growth focus is shifting to downstream solvents, fluorination chemistry and a polycarbonate JV. Near-term earnings are noisy; the long-run thesis is the China+1 specialty story.

Delhivery.desc: India's largest integrated logistics-tech company — express parcel, part-truckload, full-truckload, supply-chain services and cross-border for e-commerce, D2C and SME shippers. Crossed the FCF-positive milestone in FY26 with rising network utilisation post the Ecom Express acquisition. PTL is the swing factor for margins; volumes and yields are both inflecting.

Devyani International.desc: India's largest QSR franchisee — operates KFC, Pizza Hut and Costa Coffee stores in India, Nepal, Nigeria and beyond. Aggressive store expansion has driven scale but compressed margins; LFL recovery in KFC India and the cost-out programme are the near-term swing factors. Net store count is growing 20%+; turnaround in Pizza Hut SSSG is the watch item.

Fusion Finance.desc: Microfinance lender with operations across 22 states and a focus on rural and semi-urban income groups. Asset quality has been pressured by the post-COVID stress cycle in the MFI sector; PAR trends are beginning to stabilise. Capital position is comfortable post the FY25 fund-raise; the recovery in credit costs is the key earnings lever.

GE Vernova T&D India.desc: Indian subsidiary of GE Vernova's grid-solutions business — power transformers, high-voltage substations, GIS, HVDC and FACTS systems supplied to PGCIL, state utilities and private generators. Beneficiary of the multi-decade transmission cycle in India (renewables integration, HVDC build-out, T&D modernisation). Recent quarters saw beats on both margin and order book; the LT story is positive with PT raised.

Gland Pharma.desc: India's largest pure-play generic-injectables exporter to US, EU, Canada, Australia and emerging markets — a contract-development and manufacturing platform for sterile injectables. Reverse-merged with Fosun in 2017; turnaround in the US business and the Cenexi (France) acquisition for sterile-fill capacity are the two execution swing factors. Mar-Q materially beat estimates as the US pricing pressure eased.

Global Health (Medanta).desc: Operator of Medanta hospitals in Gurugram, Lucknow, Patna, Indore and Noida — among India's leading tertiary and quaternary care chains with strong oncology, cardiology and transplant programmes. New units (Noida, Patna ramp-up) are entering the growth-acceleration phase, driving ARPOB and EBITDA leverage. JPMorgan upgraded to OW citing the unit-mix mix shift.

Hindalco.desc: Aditya Birla group's flagship metals company — India's largest aluminium and copper producer plus the global Novelis platform in flat-rolled aluminium products. Novelis (US) is the swing factor (auto, packaging, aerospace end-markets); the India business is among the lowest-cost aluminium smelters globally. Mar-Q saw a fire-impact disruption at Novelis that's now normalising; Q4FY26 allayed most investor concerns.

Hindustan Aeronautics.desc: India's largest aerospace and defence PSU — designs and manufactures fighter aircraft (Tejas LCA), helicopters (LCH, ALH, LUH), engines, avionics and MRO services. Order book at a record ~25x book-bill on the back of large IAF orders (Tejas Mk1A, AMCA prototypes) plus follow-on helicopter contracts. Execution capacity ramp-up is the key monitorable.

ICICI Prudential Life Insurance.desc: Joint venture between ICICI Bank and Prudential PLC, among India's largest private life insurers with a balanced ULIP-protection-annuity mix. Parent shareholder Prudential PLC confirmed a stake reduction to fund its acquired-life-insurance ambitions; near-term stock overhang is real. Underlying VNB margin and APE growth remain in line with the broader sector.

ITC Hotels.desc: ITC's hotels business demerged into a separate listing — luxury and upper-upscale chain (ITC Grand, ITC Royal, WelcomHotel, Mementos, Storii, Fortune) with 140+ properties across India and select overseas. Beneficiary of the post-pandemic Indian travel surge; near-term FTA softness drove a weak Mar-Q. ARR pricing power and asset-light owned-and-managed growth are the long-term levers.

India Macro.desc: Sector notebook covering India macro indicators — CPI, IIP, GDP, fiscal deficit, RBI policy, currency, oil & commodity exposure. Aggregates broker views, RBI/MoSPI releases and the IMF/IFS macro feed used in the Macro tab snapshot.

India Strategy.desc: Sector notebook collating India-strategy reports from broker research houses — quarterly earnings dissectors, sector rotation calls, model-portfolio changes and valuation frameworks.

Indian Banks.desc: Sector notebook on Indian banking — large private banks (HDFC, ICICI, Axis, Kotak), PSU banks, asset-quality cycle, NIM trajectory, deposit competition and loan-growth mix across retail, SME and corporate.

Indian Cement.desc: Sector notebook on Indian cement — Big-5 consolidation (UltraTech, Ambuja-ACC, Shree, Dalmia, JK), pricing discipline, regional supply-demand, infra/housing demand drivers and clinker capacity additions.

Indian Financials.desc: Sector notebook for India financials — banks, NBFCs, life and general insurance, asset-management and capital-markets businesses. Tracks system credit growth, deposit-LDR dynamics and the BFSI monthly indicators.

Indian Hotels.desc: IHCL operates the Taj, SeleQtions, Vivanta, Ginger and Tree of Life brands across India and key gateway markets — over 200 hotels and a long pipeline of asset-light openings. ARR pricing power and occupancy at multi-year highs; April RevPAR growth is improving with Goa leading. Asset monetisation (Apollo Hospitals stake, others) is unlocking capital for the next leg of growth.

Indian IT.desc: Sector notebook on Indian IT services — Tier-1 (TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCL, Tech Mahindra), Tier-2 (Coforge, Persistent, LTIMindtree, Mphasis, LTTS, Cyient) and the discretionary-spend / AI-led-transformation cycle.

Indian Jewellery.desc: Sector notebook on Indian organised jewellery — Titan/Tanishq, Kalyan, Senco, PNG, Joyalukkas — covering gold price cycle, hallmarking regulation, store expansion and the unorganised-to-organised market-share shift.

Indian Oil Corporation.desc: India's largest oil-marketing and refining company — ~30% market share in fuels retail, ~80 mmtpa refining capacity and an extensive cross-country pipeline network. Beneficiary of higher inventory gains in Mar-Q with strong refining margins; greater refining exposure than peers cushions marketing-margin pressure. Capex on petchem (Paradip), green-hydrogen and gas pipelines continues.

Indian Pharmaceuticals.desc: Sector notebook for Indian pharma — generic exporters (Sun, Cipla, Lupin, Aurobindo, Dr Reddy's, Zydus), domestic-formulations leaders (Mankind, Torrent, Alkem) and CDMO/CRO names. Tracks USFDA inspection cadence, GxMeter pricing and India MAT growth.

Indian Steel.desc: Sector notebook on Indian steel — Tata Steel, JSW Steel, SAIL, Jindal Steel & Power, plus regional players. Tracks HRC pricing, coking-coal cycle, capacity additions and import/export dynamics.

Indraprastha Gas.desc: Delhi-NCR's leading city-gas-distribution company — supplies CNG to vehicles and PNG to households, commercial and industrial customers across Delhi, Noida, Greater Noida, Ghaziabad, Karnal and Rewari. Volumes are sensitive to APM gas allocation; recent CNG price hikes restored margins. The medium-term thesis is rising EV substitution in 2W/3W vs CNG growth in 4W and HCV.

JSW Energy.desc: JSW Group's integrated power utility — coal, hydro, solar, wind and a growing battery-storage / green-hydrogen portfolio. Targets ~20 GW operating capacity by FY30, evenly split between renewables and thermal. Recent acquisitions (KSK Mahanadi PPA, Mytrah Energy renewables, JV with JSW Neo) accelerated the renewable build-out.

KEC International.desc: RPG-group flagship EPC contractor — power-transmission lines, substations, railways, civil, cables and oil & gas pipelines across India, the Middle East, Africa and the Americas. Order book is at a record ~₹363bn but execution is being hit by West Asia tensions, labour shortages and payment delays in water projects. Nomura downgraded to Neutral on the soft FY27 guidance.

KIMS.desc: Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences — South India's leading multi-specialty hospital chain with anchors in Hyderabad and growing presence in Kerala, Karnataka and Maharashtra via greenfield and brownfield additions. Cluster strategy (new clusters in BLR, MUM, KOL) is the medium-term growth lever; current quarter saw new-unit drag on margins.

MakeMyTrip.desc: India's largest online travel platform — flights, hotels, holidays, bus and rail bookings across MakeMyTrip, Goibibo and redBus. US-listed (NASDAQ); business is sensitive to discretionary travel spend and currency. Near-term Middle East and oil-price headwinds drove a JPM PT cut from $110 to $60 with structural OW stance intact.

Mankind Pharma.desc: India's #4 pharma company by domestic prescriptions — strongest in chronic therapies (cardiac, anti-diabetic, anti-infective) with mass-market consumer brands (Manforce, Prega News, Gas-O-Fast). Bharat Serums acquisition added the women's health and critical-care portfolio. Q4FY26 saw a revenue miss but margins came in ahead.

NHPC.desc: India's largest hydro-power generator — operates 8 GW across 24 stations with another 4-5 GW under construction including the marquee Parbati-II and Subansiri-Lower projects. RegEq growth +25% YoY in FY26 driven by new project commissioning; delay in Parbati-II tariff is the near-term swing factor. Diversifying into solar, BESS and green hydrogen via the NHPC Renewable Energy subsidiary.

Nagarjuna.desc: Hyderabad-based mid-cap EPC contractor (also known as NCC Ltd) executing buildings, transport, electrical, irrigation, water and metals projects. Order book provides 3-year revenue cover; FY27E caution persists as receivables and working capital remain stretched.

Neogen Chemicals.desc: India's largest bromine-based specialty chemicals producer with a fast-growing organo-lithium and electrolyte-additives portfolio targeting lithium-ion battery supply chains. Capacity expansion programme nearly complete; commercial ramp-up of battery materials is the swing factor for FY27-28.

Orkla India.desc: Indian arm of Norway's Orkla group — owner of MTR Foods (South Indian ready-meals, spices), Eastern Condiments and Rasoi Magic. Recently IPO-listed; growth playbook is premium South Indian foods plus export to the diaspora. Q4 review showed volume softness in Kerala distribution reset and weak overseas.

Power Grid.desc: State-owned monopoly transmission utility — operates ~178,000 ckm of EHV lines, India's central transmission system. FY26 capitalisation beat at ~₹282bn (+213% YoY); FY27/28 capex/capitalisation guidance retained. Long-term opportunity in HVDC, GEC corridors and intra-state T&D is structurally robust; valuations are full.

Premier Energies.desc: Hyderabad-based integrated solar manufacturer — cells, modules and EPC services with ~5 GW module / 2 GW cell capacity expanding to ~10/5 GW by FY27. Beneficiary of India's PLI programme and rising domestic-content requirements (ALMM/DCR). Mar-Q operating performance beat estimates with improved solar outlook supportive of the stock.

ReNew.desc: US-listed independent power producer — India's largest by operating renewable capacity (>10 GW utility-scale wind + solar) with growing manufacturing (solar PV) and C&I business. Recent fund-raises at compelling valuations highlight asset value vs the depressed listing price. Project commissioning continues to be strong; earnings are impacted by transmission-curtailment issues.

Restaurant Brands Asia.desc: Master franchisee of Burger King in India and Indonesia — currently undergoing brand-extension into Popeyes (premium chicken QSR). India SSSG turned positive after the menu reset; Indonesia continues to be a drag with restructuring in progress.

S H Kelkar and Company.desc: India's leading domestic fragrance & flavour producer — captive serves FMCG, personal-care and home-care customers across India and ~50 export markets. Margin compression in FY26 from input-cost inflation and capacity ramp; the FY28 turnaround story is the key thesis.

SJVN.desc: Central PSU operating ~2.1 GW of hydro power across Himachal, Bhutan and Nepal — expanding into thermal, solar, wind and pumped-storage with a ~25 GW target by FY30. Earnings have been one-off-driven; project execution at scale remains the swing factor.

Siemens Energy India.desc: Demerged Siemens India energy business — high-voltage T&D, gas turbines, generators and digital-grid solutions. Export-led growth is the key positive driver; turbine and HVDC competitive intensity keep JPMorgan at Neutral. Beneficiary of India's transmission cycle and global Western-OEM diversification.

Steel Authority of India.desc: India's largest steel PSU — integrated plants at Bhilai, Bokaro, Rourkela, Durgapur, IISCO and special-steels plants. FY26 earnings beat on lower costs; volume growth visibility is soft until FY31 as expansion at Bhilai and other plants is staggered. JPMorgan flagged debt reduction as a positive.

TCS.desc: Tata Consultancy Services — India's largest IT exporter and a top-3 global IT services firm with deep banking, retail, manufacturing and life-sciences verticals. FY26 revenue exit gave a buffer for FY27 against macro headwinds; margins face larger productivity commitments, wage hikes and M&A drag. AI execution requires contextual systems-knowledge — areas where TCS sees competitive advantage.

Tata Steel.desc: Tata group's integrated steelmaker — India operations (~21 mmtpa), Europe (Netherlands ~7 mmtpa, UK transitioning to EAF), plus mining and downstream-products businesses. Mar-Q EBITDA beat on stronger realisations; domestic HRC price recovery underway. Netherlands going-concern overhang persists; capex on Kalinganagar Phase-II nearing completion.

Timken.desc: Indian subsidiary of US Timken Co — supplies tapered roller, cylindrical and spherical bearings to railways (LHB coaches, Vande Bharat), trucks, off-highway equipment and process industries. Improving performance with rising railway-capex tailwinds; export growth is the optionality.

United Spirits.desc: Diageo India's listed spirits business — owns Royal Challenge, Signature, McDowell's, plus distributes Johnnie Walker and other Diageo brands locally. Premiumisation playbook + 'three Indias' demographic-shift thesis underpin double-digit growth aspirations. Near-term volumes and margins face state-level excise-pricing volatility.

Uno Minda.desc: Tier-1 auto-components supplier — switches, lighting, horns, EV power-electronics (drive-units, BMS, motors), seat assemblies and infotainment to OEMs in India and globally. EV order wins (e.g., PV powertrain plant with anchor customer) keep growth visibility high. Near-term margins compressed by RM inflation and new-plant ramp; FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 11% ±50bp.

Vodafone Idea.desc: India's #3 wireless operator (~22% revenue share) — capex-constrained relative to Jio/Bharti; absence of bank funding remains the binding constraint. Promoter Aditya Birla Group recently agreed to infuse Rs47.3bn via preferential warrants at Rs11/share; government also reduced AGR dues to Rs640bn. ARPU growth and tariff hikes are the swing factors; JPM and Nomura stay UW/Neutral.

Zee Entertainment.desc: India's largest listed broadcaster — Zee TV linear network plus Zee5 streaming and a regional-language portfolio. Recent EBITDA loss highlighted the structural ad-market pressure on linear TV; cost-out programme and digital-monetisation pivot are the key levers.

Zydus Lifesciences.desc: Ahmedabad-based generic pharma — large US generics business, growing domestic-formulations franchise (Zydus Wellness consumer-healthcare), biosimilars and an emerging NCE pipeline. Mar-Q ahead of estimates; FY27 guidance strong. Multiple brokers retain BUY with upside contingent on US pipeline (Asacol HD, gRevlimid) execution.
